quests.question: The advisory board that reviews these applications ___ its recommendations by the end of the month.
quests.hint: 'That reviews these applications' describes the board - the true subject is still one singular body.
quests.explanation: 'The advisory board' is a singular collective noun; 'applications' inside the relative clause is just a distractor. The verb takes -s: 'submits'.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun

quests.question: A majority of the committee members who attended the hearing ___ undecided.
quests.hint: 'A majority of' agrees with the noun that follows 'of' - check whether that noun is countable and plural.
quests.explanation: 'Committee members' is countable and plural, so 'a majority of the committee members' takes a plural verb: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression + plural countable noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: The panel overseeing these decisions, along with two outside consultants, ___ holding its final session next week.
quests.hint: Ask whether 'along with' adds a second subject or just extra detail.
quests.explanation: 'The panel' is a singular collective noun; 'along with two outside consultants' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Each of the theories proposed by researchers in this field ___ its own limitations.
quests.hint: Which word is the subject: 'each', or something in the description after it?
quests.explanation: 'Each of the theories' is singular; 'proposed by researchers in this field' is just extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase

quests.question: Every conclusion drawn from the data collected across multiple trials ___ careful scrutiny.
quests.hint: Ask what 'every' does to its noun, then set the long description aside.
quests.explanation: 'Every conclusion' is singular; the phrase about data and trials is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase

quests.question: Neither of the models tested in this round of experiments ___ fully accurate.
quests.hint: Think about how 'neither of' behaves, whatever description follows.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of the models' is singular; 'tested in this round of experiments' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase

quests.question: Either the mayor, a longtime advocate for public transit, or the city council ___ expected to announce its new funding plan.
quests.hint: With 'either...or', check the noun closest to the verb - the appositive on the first noun doesn't matter.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the city council', a singular collective noun, so the verb is 'is', regardless of the appositive describing the mayor.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an appositive attached to the other noun

quests.question: Not only the residents of the flooded neighborhoods but also the local government ___ demanding immediate action from its state partners.
quests.hint: Apply the same proximity rule here, ignoring the prepositional phrase on the first noun.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the local government', a singular collective noun, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the witnesses, several of whom saw the incident, nor the officer ___ certain about the exact time.
quests.hint: Even with an embedded clause describing the witnesses, the noun closest to the verb still decides the agreement.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the officer', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an embedded phrase attached to the other noun

quests.question: The board, along with the shareholders who raised concerns last quarter, ___ scheduled to cast its vote on the proposal.
quests.hint: The shareholders and their relative clause are extra detail - the true subject is still the singular board.
quests.explanation: 'The board' is a singular collective noun; 'along with the shareholders who raised concerns last quarter' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it

quests.question: This policy, together with the amendments that were added last year, ___ under review by legal counsel.
quests.hint: Ask whether 'together with' and the clause after it can change the main subject.
quests.explanation: 'This policy' is singular; 'together with the amendments that were added last year' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it

quests.question: The agency responsible for these permits, accompanied by two independent auditors, ___ conducting a full review.
quests.hint: The auditors mentioned after 'accompanied by' don't add a second subject.
quests.explanation: 'The agency' is singular; 'accompanied by two independent auditors' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Balancing a full-time job and two young children ___ more energy than she ever expected.
quests.hint: Decide whether this gerund phrase names one activity or two.
quests.explanation: 'Balancing a full-time job and two young children' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a compound object

quests.question: To manage both the budget and the schedule for this event ___ no easy task.
quests.hint: Decide whether this infinitive phrase names one task or two.
quests.explanation: 'To manage both the budget and the schedule' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a compound object

quests.question: Juggling multiple deadlines, several of which overlap this week, ___ a serious challenge for the new intern.
quests.hint: Set the embedded phrase aside and identify the type of subject that remains.
quests.explanation: 'Juggling multiple deadlines' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'poses'.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund phrase stays singular, even with an embedded descriptive phrase

quests.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
quests.hint: Recall which word is the real subject in an 'each of' phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Each of the proposals' is singular, so the correct verb is 'is', not 'are'.
options: Each of the proposals submitted by the finalists is under review.
Each of the proposals submitted by the finalists are under review.
quests.correctAnswer: Each of the proposals submitted by the finalists is under review.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: Which version is grammatically correct?
quests.hint: 'Along with' never creates a true compound subject - check the original subject alone.
quests.explanation: 'The committee' is singular, so the correct verb is 'is', not 'are'.
options: The committee, along with several outside advisors, are finalizing its report.
The committee, along with several outside advisors, is finalizing its report.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee, along with several outside advisors, is finalizing its report.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
quests.hint: With 'neither...nor', check which noun sits closest to the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the reviewer', which is singular, so the correct verb is 'is', not 'are'.
options: Neither the researchers who conducted the study nor the reviewer is convinced by the results.
Neither the researchers who conducted the study nor the reviewer are convinced by the results.
quests.correctAnswer: Neither the researchers who conducted the study nor the reviewer is convinced by the results.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Which version is grammatically correct?
quests.hint: Ask whether the sentence is about the applicants or the count of them.
quests.explanation: 'The number of applicants' is singular, so the correct verb is 'has', not 'have'.
options: The number of applicants who meet all the requirements has increased this year.
The number of applicants who meet all the requirements have increased this year.
quests.correctAnswer: The number of applicants who meet all the requirements has increased this year.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb, even with a relative clause attached

quests.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
quests.hint: Set the parenthetical about pressure aside and identify the type of subject.
quests.explanation: 'Learning to manage a team' is a gerund phrase and is singular, so the correct verb is 'requires', not 'require'.
options: Learning to manage a team, especially under pressure, require real patience.
Learning to manage a team, especially under pressure, requires real patience.
quests.correctAnswer: Learning to manage a team, especially under pressure, requires real patience.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund phrase stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.question: Which version is grammatically correct?
quests.hint: With 'either...or', check which noun is closest to the verb - here, a relative clause is attached to it too.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the manager', which is singular, so the correct verb is 'is', not 'are' - the relative clause 'overseeing this project' doesn't change that.
options: Either the interns or the manager overseeing this project are responsible for the delay.
Either the interns or the manager overseeing this project is responsible for the delay.
quests.correctAnswer: Either the interns or the manager overseeing this project is responsible for the delay.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a descriptive phrase attached to it

quests.question: Each of the moons orbiting this planet ___ a distinct atmosphere.
quests.hint: Which word is the real subject: 'each' or 'the moons'?
quests.explanation: 'Each of the moons' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: The images captured by the telescope, along with readings from two other observatories, ___ still being processed.
quests.hint: The readings from other observatories mentioned after 'along with' don't change the true plural subject.
quests.explanation: 'The images' is plural; 'along with readings from two other observatories' is extra detail. The verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Neither the astronomers who discovered this comet nor the observatory director ___ certain about its exact trajectory.
quests.hint: With 'neither...nor', focus on the noun closest to the verb, even with a relative clause on the other noun.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the observatory director', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun

quests.question: Each of the recipes featured in this cookbook ___ locally sourced ingredients.
quests.hint: Ask which word controls the verb in an 'each of' phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Each of the recipes' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'uses'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: The head chef, along with two sous-chefs who trained in Paris, ___ preparing tonight's special menu.
quests.hint: The sous-chefs and their relative clause are extra detail - the true subject is still the singular head chef.
quests.explanation: 'The head chef' is singular; 'along with two sous-chefs who trained in Paris' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it

quests.question: Neither the appetizers listed on the menu nor the dessert ___ included in the fixed-price package.
quests.hint: Look at the last noun in the pair before the blank and check its number.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the dessert', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: The selection committee, responsible for reviewing every application that arrives before the deadline, ___ its final decision by June.
quests.hint: Bring together everything you've learned: what is the real subject, and what is only extra description?
quests.explanation: 'The selection committee' is a singular collective noun; the parenthetical phrase and the relative clause are both extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'announces'.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun stays singular, even through multiple layers of descriptive and relative-clause detail

quests.question: Neither the volunteers coordinating logistics nor the director overseeing the whole festival ___ a moment to rest this week.
quests.hint: With 'neither...nor', the noun closest to the verb decides the agreement, even with participial phrases attached to both nouns.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the director', which is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with descriptive phrases attached to both nouns

quests.question: Everyone who has followed this journey from the very beginning ___ how far the team has come.
quests.hint: One last check: how does 'everyone' behave, however the relative clause describes them?
quests.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular; 'who has followed this journey from the very beginning' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'knows'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb, even with a relative clause attached
